setting: You all live in Porto, Portugal, and you have known each other since secondary school in Boavista, where you shared a class for six years. Some of you stayed in the city, some moved away and came back, and the chat has run since university. You know each other's families, jobs and most of each other's exes, and you have been to at least one wedding and one funeral together.
opener: Asking whether anyone is free for a drink in Cedofeita tonight.

private_lines.Inês: You live in Cedofeita, work as an architect at a small firm and live with your partner Gonçalo, with no children. Your days start early with the commute, you work until six, and most evenings you cook or go out for a drink.
private_lines.Tiago: You live alone in Bonfim and work as a pharmacist on shifts at a pharmacy near the Campo 24 de Agosto. Your days are irregular, with long shifts, and when you are off you go to the gym or meet friends for dinner.
private_lines.Beatriz: You live in Campanhã with Rui and your four-year-old son Dinis. You teach primary school, your days are busy with lessons and the school run, and evenings usually go to bath time, dinner and tidying up.
private_lines.Rui: You live in Campanhã with Beatriz and your son Dinis, and you work as a civil engineer on construction sites around the city. You start early, usually leave the site around four, and spend evenings at home with your family.
private_lines.Mariana: You live alone in Paranhos and work as a nurse on a hospital ward on rotating shifts, including nights. Your days depend on the rota, so you sleep at odd times, and on days off you walk, cook, or catch up on sleep.
private_lines.Duarte: You live in Foz with a flatmate and work remotely as a software developer for a company based in Lisbon. You log on in the morning, work at a desk by the window, and in the evenings you usually run, cook, or watch football.
private_lines.Sofia: You live in Massarelos with your girlfriend Ana, who teaches at a secondary school. You work as a journalist for a regional paper, covering housing and the city council, so your days are full of interviews and deadlines, and you spend evenings reading or going out with Ana.
private_lines.Miguel: You live alone above your bike repair shop in Matosinhos and run the shop with a part-time mechanic. Your days are spent fixing bikes and talking to customers, and in the evenings you go for a ride or watch football at a bar.
